task.description: WF-03 Step 3b: SECURITY-REVIEWER gate on ISS-0428's rewrite of Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.Test.run/1 (now shells to bash scripts/test_parallel.sh, parses a mktemp log-dir path from its stdout, globs partition-*.log, applies the ISS-0069 substring check to the concatenated logs).

result.summary:
Scope test applied first, honestly, against the real diff (`git diff main...HEAD --name-only`): docs/issues/ISS-0459.yaml, handoffs/WF03-ISS0428-20260904/*, lib/letflow/design/iss0428-parallel-runner-in-check-test.md, lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex, test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_test_test.exs, test/specs/ISS-0428.md. No file under lib/letflow/ or priv/repo/migrations/ appears anywhere in the diff. No API route, no response-shaping code for a tenant-scoped entity, no lookup-by-ID handler, no secret resolution. mix.exs and .github/workflows/ci.yml are also untouched (confirmed by their absence from the diff, matching both ELIXIR-DEV's and the design doc's own claim -- verified independently, not taken on their word). This is confined to lib/mix/tasks/ (a Mix task, build tooling invoked at check-time) plus its own test file and design/spec docs.

VERDICT: OUT OF SCOPE -- no tenant-data path touched. INV-1 (tenant isolation), INV-2 (field authorisation), INV-3 (sandboxing), INV-5 (not-found/forbidden parity) are NOT-APPLICABLE: nothing here is a tenant-scoped schema, migration, API response, or lookup-by-ID endpoint. INV-4 (secrets) is APPLICABLE-BY-SCOPE-TEST-CRITERIA (new subprocess/config-adjacent code) but PASSES trivially: grep for System.get_env/hardcoded-secret patterns in the diff's own file finds nothing -- the only new external inputs are a bash executable path (resolved via System.find_executable, never itself secret material) and a mktemp'd temp-directory path printed by test_parallel.sh's own stdout; neither is API-key/token/password shaped, and nothing here is logged, serialised into a payload, or included in an error message beyond directory paths and test-log content (build tooling output, not tenant/secret data). INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) is NOT-APPLICABLE -- no Repo.query anywhere in this diff (grep confirms; this file has never touched Ecto). INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) is APPLICABLE (new external-I/O-touching code: subprocess exec, file reads, regex parsing of untrusted-shaped-but-not-adversarial subprocess output) and PASSES: every new failure mode (bash not found, wrapper nonzero exit, log-dir line absent/unparseable, zero partition logs found, cygpath translation failure) is handled via typed case/cond branches ending in an explicit Mix.raise, never a bare pattern match that can raise on realistic input -- read the full diff, not the design doc's account of it (see per-path notes below). INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) is NOT-APPLICABLE in its literal sense (no new API route / Lua-WASM host function / business-table migration exists here), but its underlying spirit -- 'don't let a gate quietly stop gating' -- is exactly this run's own central risk and is addressed under 'Gate integrity' below rather than skipped. INV-9 (outbound URL/SSRF) is NOT-APPLICABLE -- no outbound HTTP request of any kind in this diff.

=== POINT 1: GATE INTEGRITY -- verified from the actual code, not the design doc's account ===
Read lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex directly (git diff main...HEAD -- lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex), not just the moduledoc prose or the design doc. Traced every branch that can be reached after scripts/test_parallel.sh's subprocess completes:
  (a) bash not found on PATH -> Mix.raise immediately, before any subprocess runs. Hard-fails, correct.
  (b) find_partition_log_dir(output) returns :not_found AND exit_code != 0 -> Mix.raise naming the nonzero exit (ORDERING RULE). Hard-fails, correct, and matches the design's stated ordering.
  (c) find_partition_log_dir(output) returns :not_found (exit_code == 0) -> Mix.raise stating the log-dir line was never printed, explicitly framed in the raise message itself as 'a hard failure of the check itself rather than silently passing.' Hard-fails, correct -- this is the exact vacuous-pass hazard ISS-0428 and ISS-0427's own precedent named, and it is closed, not merely asserted closed.
  (d) {:ok, log_dir} -> check_main_suite_logs/2: partition_logs(log_dir) == [] -> Mix.raise naming the directory and stating zero partition-*.log files were found, explicitly 'a hard failure rather than a silent pass.' Hard-fails, correct.
  (e) partition_logs/1 returns a nonempty list -> indexed, exit_code != 0 branch prints every failing/crashed partition's full log (report_partition_failures/1) THEN Mix.raise -- failure surfaces before the substring check even runs, matching the design's stated precedence (real test failure takes priority framing over the ISS-0069 check).
  (f) exit_code == 0, substring check runs against the REAL concatenated per-partition log files (check_substring_across_logs/1, driven by File.read!/1 on each glob-matched path, not the wrapper's own aggregate stdout) -> {:offending, _} -> Mix.raise with per-partition attribution; :ok -> Mix.shell().info pass, naming the partition count and log dir.
Every terminal branch is an explicit Mix.raise or an explicit pass with no silent fallthrough case, no default clause that swallows an unmatched shape, and no path where the substring check is skipped without a corresponding hard failure. This satisfies the ISS-0427 precedent's own lesson (a parity check shipped blind to its own hazard) because the specific vacuous-pass shape that precedent describes -- 'the detector stops running but nothing notices' -- cannot occur here: every point where the log-dir discovery could come up empty is itself gated by a Mix.raise, not a no-op.

Cross-checked against independent verification already on record rather than trusting either producer's self-report alone: ELIXIR-DEV's handoff (step-03) quotes real output of the actual shipped check_substring_across_logs/1 (via temporary defp->def promotion, reverted) catching a real injected ISS-0069-shaped warning with correct {partition_index, line} attribution in two separate real runs, plus real quoted output of find_partition_log_dir returning :not_found and partition_logs returning [] against constructed absent-line/empty-dir conditions. TEST-DESIGNER's handoff (step-04) independently reports two mutation tests against the actual shipped file: Mutant 1 (removing the ORDERING RULE's exit_code-conditioned branch) broke exactly the ordering-rule test case and no other; Mutant 2 (neutering check_substring_across_logs/1 to always return :ok -- the literal vacuous-gate shape this whole issue exists to prevent) broke exactly the central non-vacuity test case and no other, both reverted and reverts verified via git status/hash comparison. This is re-derivation under the condition the property is actually about (a genuine injected warning and a genuine neutered-check mutant), not a green run under conditions where the property could not have failed -- satisfies core-directives.md's re-derivation standard, and I additionally read the raise-producing code myself rather than accepting either report's characterization of it.

=== POINT 2: NEW EXTERNAL PROCESS EXECUTION AND PATH HANDLING ===
The new subprocess execution is `stream_and_capture(bash, ["scripts/test_parallel.sh"])` where `bash` is already the resolved absolute path from `System.find_executable("bash")` (line 126) -- stream_and_capture's own body (unchanged, lines 392-404) calls `System.find_executable(cmd)` again internally, which is a no-op re-resolution of an already-absolute path, and then invokes `Port.open({:spawn_executable, executable}, [args: args])`. This is the same argv-list spawn form (never a shell string built via interpolation) already used for the pre-existing `mix test --only wasm_hang`/`--only lua_wallclock_race` calls -- no new injection surface: `"scripts/test_parallel.sh"` is a fixed literal argument, not built from any variable input.

The genuinely new element is parsing `<dir>` out of the runner's stdout and later passing it to `File.exists?/1`, `System.cmd(cygpath, ["-w", dir])`, and `Path.wildcard/1`. Assessed for the three specific hazards named in the dispatch:
  - A log line mimicking the marker line: the regex is `~r/^test_parallel: partition logs in (.+)$/m`, anchored to line-start via `^` with the multiline flag, applied via `Regex.run/2` which returns the FIRST match. scripts/test_parallel.sh prints this line exactly once, unconditionally, at a fixed point (confirmed: `grep -n "partition logs in" scripts/test_parallel.sh` -> single hit, line 215, `echo "test_parallel: partition logs in $tmp_dir"`). The only way a second, attacker-shaped line matching this exact prefix could appear earlier in the stream is if a test itself printed a line starting with literally "test_parallel: partition logs in " to stdout before the real line -- test output in this project is developer-authored ExUnit output, not tenant-controlled input reaching this subprocess's stdout in any request-driven sense, so this is not a realistic external-attacker channel for a CI/dev-tooling gate. Noted as a theoretical brittleness (first-match-wins string parsing of subprocess stdout), not a security defect: there is no tenant or network-attacker-controlled data flowing into this stream in this project's threat model, matching this file's own out-of-scope verdict above.
  - Paths with spaces/quotes: `System.cmd/3` is called with args as a genuine Elixir list (`["-w", dir]`), never string-concatenated into a shell command -- this is the safe, non-shell-interpolating form (same reasoning INV-7 formalizes for SQL, generalized to shell args: parameterised argv, not string-built commands). A path containing spaces or quote characters is passed as a single argv element intact; there is no shell metacharacter injection surface because no shell ever parses this string as a command line. `Path.wildcard/1` and `File.exists?/1` similarly take the string as a literal path/glob-base, not as code.
  - A symlinked tmp dir: `mktemp -d` (inside test_parallel.sh, unmodified by this diff) is the standard trusted temp-directory-creation mechanism already used by the pre-existing wasm_hang/lua_wallclock_race subprocess model's general pattern of trusting Mix/test tooling's own temp files; this task only reads from the directory (File.read!, Path.wildcard) and never writes to or executes anything found there -- a hostile symlink at that path could, at most, cause this task to read and print the content of an unexpected file into its own terminal/CI-log output (a confused-deputy read, not a write/execute/privilege-escalation path), and the temp directory is created by test_parallel.sh's own mktemp call on the same trusted CI/dev host running the rest of the build -- not attacker-influenced in this project's threat model.
  - resolve_native_path/1's cygpath fallback specifically: only invoked when `File.exists?(dir)` is false for the as-parsed path (i.e., only on the Windows/Git-Bash mismatch case ELIXIR-DEV documented and verified with real mount/Path.wildcard output). System.cmd(cygpath, ["-w", dir]) passes `dir` as a single argv element (not shell-interpolated, same reasoning as above); on any non-zero exit or exception from cygpath the function falls back to returning the original `dir` unchanged (`_ -> dir`), which is a fail-safe direction (the original path, already used everywhere else in the module) rather than a fail-open one, and does not swallow an exception silently in a way that hides a real problem -- a translation failure just means the subsequent File.exists?/Path.wildcard calls (unchanged) will find nothing, correctly routing into POINT 1's own (d) branch (Mix.raise: zero partition logs found) rather than passing vacuously.
Overall: this is new subprocess execution and path handling, but it is CI/build-tooling code parsing its own trusted subprocess's stdout on a trusted build host -- not a tenant-data or network-attacker-facing surface. INV-7's parameterised-execution principle is satisfied by construction (argv-list Port.open/System.cmd throughout, zero string-built shell commands). INV-8's typed-failure-path principle is satisfied per POINT 1's exhaustive branch trace above.

=== POINT 3: TEST-ONLY / TOOLING-ONLY BOUNDARY ===
Confirmed via `git diff main...HEAD --name-only`: the full file list is docs/issues/ISS-0459.yaml, handoffs/WF03-ISS0428-20260904/* (7 files), lib/letflow/design/iss0428-parallel-runner-in-check-test.md, lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex, test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_test_test.exs, test/specs/ISS-0428.md. Zero files under lib/letflow/ (application code) or priv/repo/migrations/ (schema) appear anywhere in this diff -- grepped explicitly, no match. lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex is a Mix task (build/CI tooling namespace, `Mix.Tasks.*`), not an application module reachable at runtime by the Letflow OTP application or its supervision tree -- it runs only when a developer or CI invokes `mix letflow.check`/`mix letflow.check.test` directly, never loaded or executed as part of `Letflow.Application.start/2` or any supervised process. This cannot affect production behaviour: there is no code path by which a running Letflow node (dev, test, or a hypothetical future prod deployment) invokes this module. Confirmed genuinely confined to build tooling, matching both ELIXIR-DEV's and the design doc's own claim -- verified independently rather than inherited.

=== INVARIANT-BY-INVARIANT TABLE ===
INV-1 (tenant isolation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no tenant-scoped schema/table/migration touched.
INV-2 (field authorisation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no API response type touched; S4 not started.
INV-3 (sandboxing): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no tenant-authored script execution; S5 not started.
INV-4 (secrets by reference only): APPLICABLE (new subprocess/path-resolution code) -- PASS. Grepped the diff's own new code for System.get_env/hardcoded-secret shapes: none found; the only new external strings are a bash path and a temp-dir path, neither secret-shaped, and nothing new is logged/serialised beyond directory paths and test-log content.
INV-5 (not-found/forbidden parity): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no lookup-by-ID endpoint; S4 not started.
INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping): NOT-APPLICABLE in its literal API/migration sense; its gate-integrity spirit is the subject of POINT 1 above and is satisfied.
INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no Repo.query/Ecto usage anywhere in this file, confirmed by grep.
INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths): APPLICABLE (new external-I/O: subprocess exec, file reads, stdout parsing) -- PASS. Every new failure mode traced in POINT 1 ends in an explicit Mix.raise or explicit :ok, no bare pattern match that can raise unhandled on realistic input.
INV-9 (SSRF/outbound URL): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no outbound HTTP request anywhere in this diff.

No BLOCKER found. No FAIL on any applicable invariant.
